segments: The Chronography of Barhebraeus.
144 His father had the crown placed upon him for four years.
Because from the time his wife Thecla died and he took another,
he no longer wore the crown,
nor did he sit upon the royal throne,
for a twice-married man does not rule over the Romans.
Moreover, as for his second wife, whom he had taken from a monastery,
when he died,
she shaved her head again and entered a monastery.
At this time, certain Muslim Kurds rebelled against the Arabs,
because the Mahdi, the king who was expected, appeared to them.
This man used to cast a veil over his face,
and called himself Christ and the Holy Spirit.
And crowds gathered to him,
and he fortified himself in the mountains of the land of the Kurds.
And even al-Ma'mun feared him,
and sent against him Hassan, the commander of the army.
And he subdued him in Tur Abdin while he was plundering the monastery of Qartamin.
And the Kurds were broken,
and the Mahdi fled to the land of Isaac son of Akhud the Armenian.
And Isaac seized him
and cut off his head.
Then the Kurds gathered again and encamped against {OCR?} the fortress of this Isaac,
while he happened to be away outside.
And those inside the fortress were greatly terrified.
Now a monk, the brother of Isaac's wife, when he saw that the Kurds were close to entering the fortress,
took a spear and threw himself down from the wall,
and rushed toward the chief of the Kurds, stabbed him, and killed him;
and he re-entered the fortress completely safe.
And when night fell,
the people inside had no other hope except weeping and groans to God that He might deliver them.
Even that chaste woman, the wife of Isaac, with her suckling son,
the whole night threw him before the Lord, while he was crying and she was weeping.
And at morning time, Isaac arrived with his valiant army.
And when the Kurds turned their backs to flee,
they were hindered by the snow.
And thus the majority of them were destroyed and slain;
and the few who escaped set up {OCR?} for themselves Aaron as chief,
and Ali killed him,
and after him, Babek the cattle-herdsman.
And many of them fled to Theophilos, king of the Romans.
And the Bulgarians {OCR?} also were subjected to him.
And he gathered them,
and went out and attacked Sozopetra {OCR: Nubatra} and breached it.
And he killed the men in it,
and took the women and children captive,
and burned it and returned.
And the Arabs rebuilt it again.
